result:
The last light of the day slid across the table like a slow tide, turning the wood grain into a map of rivers no one had named. I sat with an empty cup and watched it, thinking how most of what we call ordinary is just the residue of something once astonishing that we stopped noticing. A cup. A window. The particular way dust chooses which sunbeam to ride.

Somewhere a clock measured the hour into smaller and smaller pieces until the pieces themselves became the hour. I wondered whether time is a substance we move through or a habit we invented so the world would hold still long enough for us to look at it. Both answers felt true and neither one settled.

Outside, a single crow crossed the sky with the unhurried certainty of a creature that has never been asked to justify its route. It vanished behind a roof and the sky closed over the place where it had been, seamless, as if the bird had been a temporary correction the air decided to erase. I kept watching the empty patch anyway. Some absences are more precise than presence.

I thought of all the sentences that will never be finished, the ones that begin in someone’s mouth and dissolve before they reach another ear. They still exist, I decided, in the same way unplayed music exists inside an instrument left in a closed room. The potential is not nothing. It is simply waiting for a different kind of attention.

The light thinned. The table went back to being only wood. I stood, carried the cup to the sink, and let the water run longer than necessary, listening to the small, ordinary music of it. Somewhere the crow was already somewhere else, and the day, having spent itself completely, left the evening to begin again from zero.
